harmonicFunction: Bbm7 (v7) - Minor dominant starting the progression on an ambiguous, laid-back mood
Ebm9 (i9) - Emotional minor tonic with major 9th (F) adding sophisticated neo-soul warmth
Abm9 (iv9) - Minor subdominant moving smoothly along the cycle of fourths
Db9 (VII9) - Dominant 7th acting as secondary dominant to Gbmaj9
Gbmaj9 (IIImaj9) - Relative major resolution offering a fleeting, radiant release of tension
Fm7b5 (iiø7) - Half-diminished chord forming the critical jazz ii chord in the minor cadence
Bb7b9 (V7b9) - Tension-packed dominant turnaround chord with flat-9 resolving forcefully to Ebm9

techniques.name: Fingerstyle Chord Plucking
techniques.description: Simultaneous four-finger chord attack (thumb on bass, fingers 1-3 on treble strings) producing a tight, percussive pop

notes: Replaces traditional pick strumming with simultaneous finger pinching
Thumb plucks the root note while index, middle, and ring fingers pluck strings 4, 3, and 2
Allows instantaneous cut-off (choke) by placing fingers back onto the strings
Creates the tight, punchy rhythm guitar tone essential to neo-soul and modern funk
Leaves pinky free to hammer-on vocal-like 9th and 11th chord extensions
sequence: Fret the Bbm7 chord grip at the 6th fret
Assign thumb to 6th string, index to 4th, middle to 3rd, and ring to 2nd string
Pinch all 4 fingers simultaneously toward the palm
Immediately relax fretting hand pressure to create an eighth-note staccato chop
Slide smoothly to the Ebm9 grip on the next beat
tips: Keep finger movements compact—pluck upward into the hand rather than pulling away from the guitar
Mute the unplayed 5th string with the underside of your fretting thumb or index finger
Focus on making all 4 notes speak at the exact same millisecond
Use the flesh of the fingertips rather than nails for a warm, round soul attack
Practice with a metronome clicking on 2 and 4 to lock into the jazz backbeat
details.progression: Simultaneous pluck across Bbm7 - Ebm9 - Abm9 - Db9

techniques.name: Rhythmic Displacement & Neo-Soul Swing
techniques.description: Playing slightly behind the beat with a subtle 16th-note swing feel inspired by hip-hop producer J Dilla

notes: The rhythm sits in the pocket between straight eighths and swung triplets (the 'drunken' swing)
Chords are struck milliseconds after the downbeat to create a relaxed, heavy groove feel
Requires extreme rhythmic discipline to stay behind the beat without dragging the tempo
Syncopated chord releases mirror the snare drum snap
Defines the modern London jazz and neo-soul sound pioneered by Tom Misch
sequence: Set metronome to 94 BPM with swing eighth-note subdivision
Clap along with the metronome, aiming slightly behind each click
Play the Bbm7 chord on the 'and' of beat 1 rather than the downbeat
Keep fretting hand relaxed to allow micro-pauses between chord changes
Record yourself playing with the original drum loop to check pocket placement
tips: Bob your head or tap your heel to feel the sixteenth-note grid inside your body
Do not rush to the next chord—let the silence between chords groove
Listen to J Dilla's Donuts and D'Angelo's Voodoo to internalize the swung micro-timing
Keep the right wrist completely relaxed to avoid rigid mechanical attacks
If you feel like you are dragging, check that your downbeats still line up with the kick drum
details.progression: Swung pocket over Gbmaj9 - Fm7b5 - Bb7b9

techniques.name: Double-Stop Hammer-Ons & Slides
techniques.description: Hendrix-style fourth-interval and sixth-interval embellishments decorating chord shapes with lyrical melodic movement

notes: Fretting hand pinky and ring fingers decorate stationary barre chords with melodic double-stops
Focuses on perfect fourth intervals across strings 3 and 4, and strings 2 and 3
Combines chromatic approach slides from one half-step below
Bridges the gap between rhythm guitar comping and expressive lead playing
Uses Stratocaster Position 4 (neck + middle) for the signature hollow bell tone
sequence: Hold the Ebm9 chord grip firmly
Use pinky to hammer-on from the 6th to 8th fret on the B string while holding the chord
Barre across strings 3 and 4 at the 6th fret and slide up two frets to the 8th fret
Slide back down to the 6th fret and resolve to the root note on string 5
Integrate the double-stop fill at the end of every 4-measure phrase
tips: Apply even pressure across both strings during double-stop hammer-ons
Keep the slide fast and crisp—do not linger on the intermediate notes
Use light guitar strings (0.010 - 0.046) for effortless finger bending and sliding
Keep the volume of the embellishment slightly quieter than the main vocal line
Listen to Jimi Hendrix's Castles Made of Sand for the foundational technique origin

sections.name: Intro - Signature Neo-Soul Groove
sections.description: The instantly recognizable 7-chord neo-soul cycle showcasing Tom Misch's warm Stratocaster tone and syncopated four-finger plucking
sections.progression: Bbm7 - Ebm9 - Abm9 - Db9 - Gbmaj9 - Fm7b5 - Bb7b9
notes: Neck + middle pickup position creates the scooped, quacky Stratocaster chime
Pluck all 4 chord notes simultaneously with thumb and fingers 1, 2, 3
Behind-the-beat swing feel locks tightly with the relaxed hip-hop drum loop
Staccato chokes mute each chord immediately on the backbeat

sections.name: Verse - Laid-Back Vocal Accompaniment
sections.description: Intimate comping under the vocal verses with tasteful chromatic approach slides and double-stop ornaments
notes: Softer dynamic attack to let De La Soul and Tom Misch's vocals take center stage
Subtle fourth-interval hammer-ons on the G and B strings between vocal phrases
Chromatic slide-ins from one fret below inject sweet soul character
Keep the fretting hand relaxed to ensure silent, noise-free chord transitions

sections.name: Bridge - Chromatic Extension Movement
sections.description: Harmonic transition section lifting through major 7th chords before dropping into the altered dominant turnaround
notes: Ascending chord voicings build emotional tension toward the chorus
Notice the smooth voice leading: the top melody line climbs stepwise
Fm7b5 to Bb7b9 creates the classic jazz minor ii-V turnaround
Let the altered notes (b9 and #5) ring out clearly before resolving back to Eb minor

sections.name: Outro - Extended Vamp & Guitar Solo
sections.description: Expansive groove finale featuring Tom Misch's George Benson and John Mayer-style melodic guitar solo over the looping vamp
notes: Eb Dorian scale provides the smooth minor-major hybrid soloing vocabulary
Wes Montgomery / George Benson thumb-strummed octaves for warm dynamic peak
Vocal-like string bending targeting the 9th (F) and 11th (Ab) chord tones
Subtle analog chorus and tape echo create a lush, enveloping 3D stereo spread

guitar.pickup: Position 4 (neck + middle pickups in parallel) for the classic scooped neo-soul hollow chime

settings.treble: 5.5 (warm, rolled-off highs that never sound harsh or piercing)
settings.middle: 6.0 (full, singing midrange body to support single-note lines)
settings.bass: 4.0 (tight low end to sit cleanly on top of the bass guitar)

effects.distortion: None or transparent overdrive (JHS Morning Glory / Ibanez TS808 on zero gain for mid boost)

effects.other: Optical compressor (Diamond / Keeley) set for slow attack and singing sustain; Boss CE-2W analog chorus in CE-1 mode

beginner.title: Master Extended Neo-Soul Chord Grips
steps: Memorize the fretboard shapes for Bbm7, Ebm9, Abm9, and Db9
Practice forming the half-diminished Fm7b5 shape without buzzing strings
Work on thumb-over positioning on the 6th string for stable bass anchor notes
Shift between chord grips slowly at 60 BPM with clear note ring-out
Ensure the unplayed 5th string is cleanly muted during root-6 chord grips
beginner.goals: Achieve clean muscle memory and transitions across all 7 chord shapes at 60 BPM

intermediate.title: Internalize the Laid-Back Swing Feel & Finger Pluck
steps: Adopt the four-finger pluck technique (thumb + fingers 1, 2, 3 simultaneously)
Practice muting chords immediately after the attack for a tight percussive pop
Incorporate the behind-the-beat neo-soul swing feel with a metronome at 75 BPM
Add subtle chromatic approach slides from one fret below into major and minor grips
Record yourself playing to verify note balance and laid-back pocket placement
intermediate.goals: Groove through the complete 7-chord progression at full 94 BPM with authentic pocket

advanced.title: Incorporate Hendrix Embellishments & Soloing
steps: Add double-stop 4th and 6th hammer-ons while sustaining chord root notes
Improvise over the Eb minor progression using Eb Dorian and Bb Altered scales
Master dynamic contrast between soft verse comping and expressive solo peaks
Incorporate Wes Montgomery thumb-octaves in the outro solo
Perform the entire song with natural improvisational flair and groove authority
advanced.goals: Performance-ready execution of both rhythm and lead at 94 BPM with personal stylistic touches

commonMistakes: Rushing ahead of the beat instead of sitting relaxed in the pocket behind the snare drum
Strumming with a pick instead of plucking all 4 chord notes simultaneously with thumb and fingers
Letting open strings ring unintentionally during half-diminished and altered chord grips
Using excessive distortion or overdrive which turns complex 9th and 11th chord extensions into muddy noise
Over-playing dense fills during vocal sections instead of serving the minimalist groove
practiceRoutine: 10 minutes: Extended chord grip transitions with metronome set to 2 & 4 jazz clicks
15 minutes: Four-finger pluck and release drill focusing on crisp percussive cutoffs
15 minutes: Main 7-chord progression looping at 80 BPM building to 94 BPM
10 minutes: Eb Dorian and Eb minor pentatonic double-stop fill vocabulary
10 minutes: Solo improvisation over the outro groove backing track
focusAreas: Behind-the-beat micro-timing and relaxed groove placement
Clean half-diminished and altered dominant chord voicings
Stratocaster pickup selection (Position 4) and touch dynamics
metronomeWork: Practice with metronome clicking on beats 2 and 4 only to cultivate internal swing
Start slow at 70 BPM to ensure every finger strikes precisely at the exact same instant
Increase to 85 BPM, focusing on relaxing the fretting hand during chord transitions
Target 94 BPM as the album tempo, locking into the drum kick-and-snare pocket
Practice at 90 BPM with exaggerated swing feel to deepen groove flexibility
